Defence strip · the proposal

  • Colour says one thing: good or bad for you. Green — resistance, immunity, a bonus, advantage on your roll, disadvantage on an attack against you. Red — the opposite. Grey — a sense. Gold is gone from the strip.
  • On YOUR roll the swing is the roller's triangle (.advantage-cue-up / -down), and shape and colour never disagree: up is green, down is red, as in the dice tray.
  • "Against you" keeps its words and loses its fill and its gold. The die is somebody else's, so a triangle there would point one way and mean the other; the sentence says whose swing it is, and the colour says whether that is good for you.
  • The mixed blocks add two MOCKED chips: a disadvantage on your save, and an advantage for an attacker.
